issues.title: Panicky vibes

takeaways.t: Fears over AI regulation after the Democratic midterm win sent the Nasdaq down 5.52% to more than 10% below its high, and the S&P 500 fell 4.36% in its worst day since April 2025.
The Philadelphia semiconductor index dropped over 12%, with Nvidia down 9%, Sandisk down 22%, and Palantir and CrowdStrike each down nearly 10%.
The VIX jumped 69% while gold rose more than 0.6% and Treasuries rallied, pulling the 10-year yield down 6 bps to 4.837%.
Shares fell 10.77% on worries about clashing with a bluer Texas.
The league is shutting down in bankruptcy after Saudi PIF pulled its $5 billion backing and a $300 million BC Partners rescue fell through.
The NYT is reportedly in advanced talks to buy Letterboxd for about $330 million, and Wendy's rejected a $1.4 billion buyout bid from Trian-led investors.

issues.note: Market numbers are the Nov 5 close.

issues.title: Making sense of the market plunge

takeaways.t: An AI-driven selloff pushed the Nasdaq down 5.32% into correction territory, the S&P 500 down 4.18% and the Dow down 3.33% (over 1,700 points).
Fears of tighter data-center rules after the midterms hit chipmakers: Sandisk fell 22.26%, AMD 17.26%, Nvidia 9.26%, and the VIX jumped over 60%.
Treasurys rallied as the 10-year yield fell 6 bps to 4.837%, its lowest since early September; Bitcoin dropped 5% to $76,038.
Oil rose 2.94% to $90.71 on renewed uncertainty over the Iran war.
Memory-chip costs hurt Nintendo, whose profit fell 16% as Switch 2 sales dropped 41%, while Sony's profit rose 45% and its stock gained 6.19%.
AppLovin jumped 31.04% and Warby Parker 22.59% on earnings, while Dutch Bros sank 21.41% and Snap 14.02%.
Stocks surged after Democrats swept the midterms, with the Dow up 3.03% (over 1,500 points), the S&P 500 up 1.58% and the Nasdaq up 1.44%.
The 10-year yield slipped 6 bps to 4.894% as investors bet a divided Washington will curb spending and borrowing.
Oil tumbled 7.65% to $88.74 as fears of a US attack on Iran eased.
CVS will split its retail pharmacies from Aetna and Caremark by early 2028; despite $108.4B in revenue (+5.4%) and a raised outlook, shares fell 12.53%.
Duolingo jumped 25.99% and Block 15.32% on earnings, while Amdocs dropped 30.07% and Trump Media 24.54%.
The US is projected to hit its $41.1T debt ceiling by summer 2027, and BNY expects at least one shutdown next year.
Chip stocks rebounded, lifting the Nasdaq 0.84% and S&P 500 0.35% while the Dow slipped 0.46%.
The 10-year yield rose 6 bps to 4.952% as investors waited on midterm election results.
Apple posted record revenue of $114.5B (+12%) and $2.10 EPS, but fell 1.90% after warning memory-chip costs will cut gross margin to 45%-46%.
Palantir revenue jumped 96% to $2.31B and US commercial sales topped government for the first time, yet shares lost 1.65% on slower bookings.
Shopify fell 8.74% after $3.74B revenue missed estimates, even as AI-referred orders grew 3.3x.
Fiserv surged 12.46% and Eaton gained 7.03%, while Gartner tumbled 13.28% and Dynatrace sank 14.74%.

issues.title: What the midterms mean for your portfolio

takeaways.t: An early AI rebound faded and chips reversed, leaving the Nasdaq down 1.07% and S&P 500 down 0.51% while the Dow gained 0.41%.
Oil sank 7.99% to $95.80 on US-Iran talk hopes, pulling the 10-year yield down 4 bps to 4.894%.
With divided government likely, Morgan Stanley says the S&P 500 averaged a 23% gain in the year after midterms when Congress was split.
Marvell is buying Lumentum in an all-stock deal valued at $115B; Marvell fell 12.82% and Lumentum 18.66%.
Oracle slid 8.85% on a $20B debt-and-stock raise, Intel fell 8.8%, while IDEXX jumped 21.85% and Rivian rose 8.47%.
Marriott beat estimates with $7B revenue, $3.02 adjusted EPS and raised 2026 RevPAR growth guidance to 4.5%-5%; shares rose 4.26%.

issues.title: A crypto heist like no other

takeaways.t: The tech selloff deepened, with the Nasdaq down 2.83% (off as much as 3.7% intraday) and the S&P 500 down 2.09%, while the 10-year yield eased 7 bps to 4.915%.
Intel plunged 28.58% on a weak Q4 outlook despite 21% revenue growth to $16.5B, and Amazon slipped 1.41% as free cash flow hit negative $42.4B with $220B of planned capex.
Hackers drained about $6.3B from Binance, the largest crypto heist ever, sending Bitcoin down 4.99% to $76,717, a six-week low.
Chevron earned $9.9B (+~200%) and Exxon $15.4B (doubled) on refining, lifting shares 1.75% and 2.25% with oil up 2.27% to $104.32.
Reddit fell 29.34%, Roblox 18.13% and Twilio 15.48%, while FedEx Freight rose 14.91%, Regeneron 13.33% and AstraZeneca 6.78%.
Alphabet-led tech selling pushed the Nasdaq down 1.38% and the S&P 500 down 0.30%, while the 10-year yield slipped 6 bps to 4.989% after a solid GDP print.

The stock fell 12.29%, its worst day ever and about $500B in lost value, as free cash flow hit negative $9.1B versus a negative $3.5B estimate and search revenue of $63B missed the roughly $65B forecast.
Eli Lilly rose 6.63% on $24.4B in revenue (+39%) with Mounjaro at $10.7B, and Merck gained 3.83% on $18.1B with Keytruda at $8.6B ahead of 2028 patent expirations.
DoorDash rose 5.61% on a $17B deal for Instacart, while Marvell fell 13.24% on reports of advanced talks to buy Lumentum.
ServiceNow dropped 26.64% on weak subscription guidance and Fortinet fell 20.09% on a service revenue cut, while Crocs jumped 25.54% and Carvana gained 15.59%.
With GDP up 3.4% and consumer spending up 3.8%, Chili's same-store sales rose 10.1% and Cheesecake Factory 15.2%, while Wingstop fell 5.4% and Popeyes 2.2%.
Stocks edged up as the Fed held rates, with the S&P 500 up 0.28% and Nasdaq up 0.27%, while the 10-year yield rose 5 bps to 5.045% and oil gained 1.39% to $101.29.
The Fed kept rates at 3.75%-4.00% with two of 12 members dissenting for a hike over 3.7% inflation; odds of a December hike are around 85%.
Prediction markets brought in $173M last quarter, more than six times a year ago, helping record revenue of $1.42B (+12%), but EPS missed and shares fell 3.30%.
Prediction markets traded over $14B in notional volume last weekend, a record two-day stretch, with Kalshi alone above $10B and $1.4B already traded on midterm markets.
Vertiv jumped 16.40% and Wendy’s 15.15% on a $1.4B Trian offer, while F5 fell 20.43%, Enphase 16.03% and Boston Scientific 5.84% after a guidance cut.
DoorDash is nearing a roughly $17B deal for Instacart, and the Energy Department is backing Constellation with $5B to upgrade nuclear plants.
Chip and AI hardware enthusiasm lifted the Nasdaq 1.18% and S&P 500 0.60%, while oil slid 1.90% to $99.83 on Middle East de-escalation hopes.
Shares fell over 10% as the 737 Max rate of 47 a month slips to early 2027 (about 42 now); commercial unit lost $697M and Q3 deliveries dropped to 161 from 171.
Free cash flow was $464M versus roughly $325M expected, keeping the $1B-$3B full-year target in reach despite $45.9B of debt.
Q3 sales rose 7% to $13.4B and adjusted EPS rose 11% to 91 cents; volume grew 5% and the full-year outlook was raised, with shares flat.
JetBlue jumped 18.99% on an upbeat outlook, SoFi gained 13.42% and Pentair 12.74%, while Xylem sank 14.26% and Innodata fell 25.32% after about 550 layoffs.
Full-time MBA applications fell 27% for the class of 2028; Harvard's endowment still grew over $11B on a roughly 27% return.
Filed a 318-page prospectus showing $16.3B in H1 revenue vs $1.2B a year earlier; Q3 growth slowed to 45% from 140%, and Wall Street cut its valuation target to $1.5T from $2T.
Added 406,000 postpaid phones (nearly double estimates) and raised its outlook, but a slight revenue miss sent shares down 3.38%.
Reports of a push for 80,000+ US cell sites weigh on carriers; TD Cowen pegs a national network at $80B+, and SpaceX closed a $40B Apollo financing.
EQT agreed to buy Range Resources for ~$12.8B (RRC +17.68%); Surgery Partners jumped 47.62% on a reported ~$6B Bon Secours Mercy bid.
Plans buyouts for roughly 60,000 employees, about 27% of its workforce; shares rose 1.54%.
Tesla +5.21% on a Barclays upgrade; Fair Isaac -13.15% and JetBlue -9.71%; Petrobras -13.99% and Nu -16.95% after Lula's election win.
US crude jumped 4.2% to $103.67 on Middle East fears; gold hit its lowest since July.
Record $20.1B revenue (+9%) and profit up 28% to $3.71B, but stock fell 3.7% on a slight miss and ~3,500 job cuts.
SK Hynix shelved a Solidigm US listing, Firmus scrapped its IPO, and Oura delayed its own.
Reportedly trimmed its funding target to $1.25T from $1.4T on softer demand.
AT&T fell 8% and T-Mobile 7.7% on reports SpaceX is seeking access to 80,000 cell towers.
US luxury spending fell 6% in September while high earners drove most Beige Book districts.
Nasdaq had its worst day since June.
AI spending worries. Stock split in January keeps Zuckerberg's voting control.
Fuel up 68% at American, but premium-cabin revenue is growing 17-23%.
Staples +5%, healthcare at a record, P&G +5.6%, Lockheed +6.9%.
Lam Research -11.8%. Semis had their worst week since April 2025.

issues.title: AI Stocks Crack While Retail and Energy Take the Lead

takeaways.t: A Friday chip rout made it a third straight weekly loss for the S&P 500, while the Russell 2000 was the only major index up on the week (+1.3%).
Intel fell 28.6% and the semiconductor index dropped 7.2% Friday; Amazon (-$42.4B trailing FCF), Alphabet and Meta are all burning cash on AI capex.
The Fed held at 3.75% to 4.00% with two dissents for a hike (December hike near 76%), and WTI sits at $104.12 after a 15% October gain.
Support at 7,500 then the 200-day near 7,300; resistance at 7,800. The 7,600 to 7,680 band held eight times since June.
Leaning bullish at $150.52 after a gap to 52-week highs on strong earnings. Watching the $148-150 area to join the trend; the thesis fails below $140. Better as a swing than intraday.
At $154.03 after new all-time highs on analyst upgrades. Would consider a pullback toward the 8EMA near $146-149 with risk under $145. Earnings Nov 5, and a big gap down would void the setup.
Data: ISM Mon, JOLTS Tue, ADP Wed, jobs report Fri. Earnings: AAPL and PLTR Mon; AMD, AMGN, ANET, SHOP Tue; DASH, UBER, APP, COHR Wed; ABNB, LITE, AAOI Thu.
